correctness.rationale: For any prime p=2 (mod 3) and k>a=3j with p<=2^(k+1)-1, T=2^(k+1)-1, A=(T-p)/2 and B=(T+1)/2 give a valid distinct-divisor half-partition of z=2^k p because A+pB=(p+1)T/2. For M=2^(k+1)p^2, z+tM=z(1+2pt) remains Zumkeller: the multiplier is coprime to z (odd and congruent 1 mod p) and copying the balanced divisor partition across each coprime factor balances the product. For v2(N)=3j, p∤N, N-z has exact valuation 3j modulo 2^(k+1), and its odd quotient is a cube of a 2-adic unit because 3 is invertible on each odd-unit 2-group; the p²-unit cube map is also bijective since p=2 mod3. CRT yields x mod M, choose 1<=x<=M; for N>=z+M^3, t=(N-z-x^3)/M is nonnegative. In fixed valuation stratum, failures for K distinct such primes require divisibility by their product aside from finitely many exceptions, hence density zero as K→infinity. Valuation strata density 2^-(3j+1) and summing finite j then J→infinity yields lower density 4/7, not global density existence. Independently checked four exact admissible modular cases and subset sums; these finite checks do not prove the density limit.
